title: Hero of the Mag'har: Garrosh, Geyah, and Thrall's Return
summary: Garrosh's shame leads the seeker from Garadar to Oshu'gun, Shattrath, and Auchindoun. The ancestors' danger brings a message to Thrall, whose return and account of Grom's sacrifice change the name Garrosh can bear.
opening: Beneath Nagrand’s floating islands, the Mag’har endure a history their young Hellscream cannot yet forgive. The ancestors’ unrest carries a stranger toward Geyah’s lost family, and a memory returns to Garadar that Garrosh has never heard.

chapters.title: A burden in Garadar
chapters.body:
Garadar endured beneath Nagrand’s bright sky, a home held together without the strength of the greater Horde around it. At its center stood Garrosh Hellscream, burdened by his father’s name. He remembered Grom through the corruption that had claimed him and feared the same rage within himself. Greatmother Geyah waited with an older memory. Before Garrosh could imagine a future, the weight of that past had to be heard.

Geyah welcomed the seeker as a guest of her people. Materials gathered across Outland were prepared into a potion, opening the way toward the ancestors who still walked Nagrand’s green places. Beyond the village waited Mother Kashur. Garrosh’s grief had drawn the visitor to Garadar; now the Greatmother’s counsel led toward a memory older than his sorrow.

At the Ancestral Grounds, weathered stones and a spring marked a place of listening. Mother Kashur received the seeker there. The ancestors were restless, and their meaning could not be made simple by Geyah’s preparation alone. Kashur asked that the old sites be visited and the spirits’ words brought back. The valley’s quiet held a question the living had yet to understand.

At Sunspring Post, the Laughing Skull ruins, Garadar and the Bleeding Hollow ruins, restless spirits spoke of a call from the south. Their broken words pointed toward Oshu’gun, the pale mountain that had long watched over Nagrand. Scattered unease had found a destination. Mother Kashur sent the seeker onward, toward the place drawing the ancestors beyond their familiar grounds.

chapters.title: The voices beneath the Light
chapters.body:
Oshu’gun rose among Nagrand’s grass and water like a fragment of another world. Beneath its pale mass, the ancestors’ call grew stronger. The mountain was sacred to the Mag’har, yet within its silence waited a presence whose light was failing. The search that had begun with restless whispers now reached the being toward which those lost souls were drawn.

K’ure said that its energies had ebbed over centuries, leaving a Void that consumed nearby souls. Generations of orc ancestors had been drawn into that vortex. The naaru also spoke of the Legion harnessing it to bring void minions into its ranks. Part of the cycle might still be answered. From Oshu’gun, K’ure sent the seeker toward A’dal in Shattrath.

A’dal heard K’ure’s account and answered cautiously. The ancestors’ suffering could not be lifted by a word of Light alone. Another naaru was bound to the question, and the way led toward Auchindoun. Shattrath offered direction without an easy promise of healing. Beneath Terokkar’s ruined halls, another witness might reveal what could still be done for those drawn into darkness.

In the Auchenai Crypts, D’ore explained that the cycle could not simply be stopped: without the Void, the Light could not exist. The spirits threatened by corruption had to be released before darkness consumed them. Beneath blue-grey stone, listening gave way to a difficult duty. The seeker carried a mirror through the crypts, seeking those whose change had already begun.

The Soul Mirror revealed darkened spirits among the ancient orc ancestors. The seeker defeated those already changing, before the Void could take them fully. When the work was done, Mother Kashur received the news at the Ancestral Grounds. The dead had not been restored to life. They had been given a chance to rest beyond the force that called them south.

chapters.title: A message to the Warchief
chapters.body:
Mother Kashur gave thanks for the ancestors released from the darkening cycle and sent the news back to Garadar. Geyah spoke of a people who had endured and might yet know more seasons. Then her concern turned toward Garrosh. He had heard of the seeker’s service; perhaps its meaning could reach him where the Greatmother’s comfort had not.

Geyah asked the seeker to tell Garrosh that the work had been done for him and his people. He could find little comfort in it. The clan might survive another winter, but he could not imagine a future beyond it. His family’s name remained a shame he wished to lay down, and the fear of his father’s corruption still shadowed his own worth.

Garrosh sent word to Geyah that he believed himself unfit to lead. He feared the old corruption might damn the orcs again. In the exchange that followed, Geyah learned that the Horde’s Warchief was Thrall, son of her lost child Durotan. She could not travel to him herself. The seeker would carry an urgent message: his blood still lived upon Draenor.

In Orgrimmar, the seeker delivered Geyah’s message. Thrall answered with astonishment: he had a grandmother, and she lived. Grom’s legacy remained upon the broken world as well. The summons reached beyond war or duty. Thrall would return to Nagrand to meet the family left behind when his parents had crossed the Dark Portal.

chapters.title: A memory returned
chapters.body:
At Garadar, Geyah met the grandson she had feared lost. Thrall also brought Garrosh a memory from the Third War. At Demon Fall Canyon, Grom had stood against Mannoroth and died striking the blow that broke the demon’s hold over the orcs. The corruption and its cost were not erased. Yet the father’s last choice had been hidden beneath the son’s shame.

The memory faded, leaving Garrosh in Garadar with a changed understanding of his name. Grom had broken the demon’s hold at the cost of his life. Garrosh could now call himself son of Grom and chieftain of the Mag’har with pride. Thrall honored the bond he had shared with Grom, then returned to Geyah. The Greatmother received the final news of service to her people.

reviewNote: Complete illustrated research StoryGuide with 15 scenes and source-linked events and claims. The Horde-only unlock has its actual prerequisite branches: Totem of Kar'dash/Murkblood and the Nagrand diplomacy and Forge Camp threads ending at Message to Garadar and Forge Camp: Annihilated; it does not require every Nagrand quest. The original TBC continuation includes Thrall, Son of Durotan and Hero of the Mag'har, removed in 4.0.1. Human gates: original quest/build and prerequisite-edge review; exact claim and Chronicle page review; TBC side-by-side area and model resemblance; visual composition review; and voice audition. The Third War scene is labeled as memory. The story ends before Garrosh's later career. Added to the independent Classic-to-Wrath StoryTour, not an EraTour.
